heartbeat.title: Specificity beats generic framing
heartbeat.body_html: The clearest pattern across this month's winners is that naming the specific thing outperforms vague reassurance. Subject lines that named the actual product ("your Bombers", "your shades"), the exact discount ("15% off"), a concrete deadline ("expires tonight"), or added first-name and ownership framing repeatedly beat softer, generic copy across Abandoned Cart, Back In Stock and Browse Abandon. This is a transferable lever we now apply deliberately: concrete detail and ownership language earn attention that abstract framing does not, and every one of these wins is banked permanently in the flows.

narrative.html: Flows earned $51,493 this month, up 7.3% versus July. Revenue per email delivered rose from $0.271 to $0.283, so each send is working harder, and flows held 10.4% of total store revenue.

Flows are the most efficient per-email channel we run. At $0.283 per email delivered, flows earn 12.3x what campaigns do per email ($0.023). Both are our work, and this is simply why automated flows carry the heavier load per send.

Campaigns are the second lever we run alongside flows. We sent 24 campaigns this month, and email revenue split almost evenly at 51% flows to 49% campaigns, giving Bomber a broad, always-on reach across both channels.

Deliverability stayed clean and well inside safe limits. Unsubscribes were 0.1% of delivered and spam complaints just 0.002%, which protects inbox placement and keeps every send landing where it should.

heartbeat.title: Consequence framing beats convenience framing
heartbeat.body_html: The clearest transferable lesson from July's winners is that giving the reader a concrete stake to act on outperforms softer, convenience-led messaging. In Replenishment, leading with loss aversion ("don't wait until your pair gives out") beat the easy-reorder framing, and in Bounce Back a direct consequence question ("what's your plan when they break?") beat the generic control. The same instinct showed up in the winning Welcome subject line built on specific product credentials. We are now rolling this consequence-first framing into the next round of tests across the post-purchase flows, which is how a single proven idea compounds across the whole program.

narrative.html: Flows earned $47,978, up 1.0% on the prior month, and revenue per email delivered climbed from $0.257 to $0.271. More value out of every send is the cleaner signal here, since it shows the gain came from stronger emails rather than simply more volume.

Flows held 9.5% of total store revenue, in line with the 9.0% we saw in June and consistent with the band the flows have run in across the year. Against total store sales of $503,522, that is the automated layer doing steady, always-on work in the background.

Flows are the most efficient per-email channel we run, earning 8.2x what campaigns earn per email ($0.271 vs $0.033). Campaigns are the second lever we also run, with 19 sent this month; they reach the full list on our timing while flows monetise intent one subscriber at a time. Flows drove 41% of email revenue, and the two levers do different jobs by design.

Deliverability stayed clean, with unsubscribes at 0.097% of delivered and spam complaints at 0.003%. Healthy list signals like these are what keep both the flows and the campaigns landing in the inbox month after month.
